$comment: Canonical per-domain validator checklists (#1000 / rejection-rate fix #3). The generation spine injects these into the USER prompt via src/runtime-core/ValidatorChecklist.ts. The module's inline copy is the interim verbatim copy of this file; the drift-guard test (test/unit/runtime-core/validator-checklist-drift.test.ts) fails on any divergence between the two, and on any spine-supported domain missing a checklist. Source history: PE-2's validator-checklists v1 (Forgejo #988 comment 16779, 2026-09-01).

p5: reference p5 globals (createCanvas, background, ...) — no DOM-only code
three: reference THREE.* or import from "three" (exactly ONE THREE import)
create scene, camera, renderer; call renderer.render
every light intensity <= 3.0 (key 0.8-2.0, ambient 0.25-0.6) with renderer.toneMapping = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping
scene background / clear color is a deep mid-tone (e.g. 0x2a3a4e or lighter), never near-black
glsl: one complete fragment shader with void main()
no setup()/draw() — this is raw GLSL
strudel: use strudel patterns (s("..."), note(), stack(), bpm())
do NOT prefix with $: (that is hydra notation)
tone: use the global Tone.* (already loaded) — no import statements
html: balance every tag you open (the validator checks closing tags)
NO inline on*= handlers, NO javascript: URLs
dataviz: MUST load D3.js (script tag or import) — a dataviz piece without D3 fails validation
custom: MUST include a render mount (the element your composition attaches to)
kinetic: an explicit loop or animation driver
ascii: plain ASCII art block (no code execution expected)
music: either strudel or hydra idioms (see those checklists)
textgen: return RAW TEXT (the text itself is the artwork) — NOT an HTML document
substantial output — a receipt under the minimum size fails validation
vary the line lengths — fewer than 3 distinct lengths among non-empty lines is rejected as a non-generative receipt
blender: a raw Python script that imports bpy (no HTML, no markdown fences)
no network, subprocess, shell, os file access or exec/eval — those constructs are rejected before Blender runs
build objects, a light and a camera, and set bpy.context.scene.camera
never call bpy.ops.render or set the output path: the host renders one capped still
revideo: one Revideo scene source file (TSX): export default makeScene2D("SceneName", function* (view) { ... }) — no HTML, no markdown fences
import only from @revideo/2d and @revideo/core; @revideo/react, Remotion, React.FC, useCurrentFrame, p5 setup()/draw() are rejected
nothing external: no fetch, no URL images or video, no staticFile, no Audio/Video nodes — the render is offline
the scene must animate (yield* on node signals) and end: total length between 4 and 20 seconds
nbe: one JSON object of nbe engine settings and nothing else — no HTML, no code, no markdown
palette is 3-6 hex colours darkest first, deliberately chosen for the brief; numeric fields stay inside the stated ranges
layout, emitters, fieldScale, flow and swirl are chosen so this brief looks different from a generic default
reason is one sentence saying why these settings fit the brief

libraryRules.$comment: Library legality rules enforced by src/core/validators/LibraryRulesValidator.ts (#1068) beyond the per-domain checks — carried here so prompt authors see the full contract.
rules: max 3 DISTINCT library ids per piece
culori pieces: interpolate in oklch/lab — NEVER hand-rolled hex lerp, lerpColor, or 'rgb'-space mix
rapier2d: world.timestep must be a FIXED constant (1/60) with an accumulator — never dt/clock-driven
physics (rapier/matter-js): spawn bodies in a bounded loop, ≤128 creation sites
declaration EXACT syntax, AFTER the closing code fence: libraries: id1, id2
